_comment: Address map for Sid Meier's Pirates! (2004). Verified against the binary named below. No ASLR (DllCharacteristics=0, ImageBase 0x400000) so these are absolute runtime VAs.

text_api._comment: printf-style formatter with named tokens (@NUM, @HAPPY, @NAME, @CITYNAME, @NATIONALITY, @CITYTYPE, @MONTH, @DIFFICULTY, @SHARE). Tokens consume varargs left-to-right exactly like printf. IMPORTANT: esi must equal 0x008E9F58 (the message-buffer object) before calling; the wrappers do not set it themselves.

AddText_mode0.sig: void (const char* fmt, ...)  // esi = msgbuf, internal flag 0

AddText_mode1.sig: void (const char* fmt, ...)  // esi = msgbuf, internal flag 1

Formatter_core.sig: __fastcall(ecx = fmt)(void* varargs, int flag)  // esi = msgbuf object

crew._comment: Discovered via the mutiny and 'Your crew of @NUM is @HAPPY' call sites.

gold_869AB4.note: GOLD (plunder). Read immediately after the divide-plunder text call at 0x0041032A (`mov eax,[0x869AB4]`), and it is slot 0 of the 7-entry contiguous cargo-hold array. Was 'gold or food?'; the divide-plunder read settles it.

morale_byte_869B27.note: shl 2 then subtracted in morale calc

GetCrewMoodString.note: Returns the @HAPPY substitution string. Internally computes a score clamped to [1, 999] (0x3E7).

WrapText.sig: cdecl (int width, int mode) -> int lineCount
WrapText.note: CONFIRMED 2026-08-02, and NOT a card presenter -- an earlier note guessed '(int id, int flag) ShowMessageCard'. param_1 is a COLUMN WIDTH: it pulls the message text via FUN_00412F10, wraps it with FUN_004F22C0(&s, width), strcpy's the result into the shared buffer 0x869B48 and returns the line count.

MeasureText.sig: (void* font, const char* s, char stopAtNewline) -> float10 maxLineWidth
MeasureText.note: Text MEASUREMENT, presents nothing. Walks glyph widths off the font object at +0x44; handles '\n' and '<' markup.

FitTextToWidth.note: Measures the buffer, then while it is narrower than the space available AND runs past 3 lines, widens the WrapText column by 2 and retries. Finds the narrowest wrap that fits in three lines.

PlaySoundCue.sig: (ecx, eax, esi, int soundId, int, int, float) // cdecl stack args
PlaySoundCue.note: AUDIO, NOT PRESENTATION -- proven by its own error string at 0x00709E20, 'The audio manager has not been properly initialized yet'. The int arg is a SOUND ID (0x2A news sting, 0x39 card). This function has been mistaken for a text presenter twice; FUN_00488A80 next door is the spoken-callout entry point. Read the strings in 0x4888xx-0x4889xx before naming anything there.

PostNoticeStrip.note: The game's own post to the bottom-of-screen notice strip: WrapText(0x20=32 cols), strcpy 0x869B48 -> 0x876BF8, then set the 0x8CA9E8 counter to 100. Called at 0x0044E91B after the news composer.

OverworldHudDraw.note: The sailing-screen HUD: Fame, '@NUM knots', '@NUM crew', the date, and the notice strip (gated on 0x8CA9E8, art 'tornPaper.dds', text drawn with FUN_004B06C0 in 0xFF1A3E1A).

ShipAI.note: The overworld ship AI. Reads purpose a dozen times. Contains BOTH engagement paths: the relations-based one EXCLUDES the player (`if (other != 0)`), and the target-based one at 0x0046A61E does not but is unreachable for slot 0. Neighbour scan at 0x00469DF6 starts at slot 0 or 8 depending on a bit in 0x0085A164 and does include the player as a candidate.

BuildConvoyWithEscorts.sig: (int city, int homeCity, int shipType, int escortNation, int kind)
BuildConvoyWithEscorts.note: Builds a ship, then N privateers (purpose 2) whose pursuit target is that ship. The only writer of +0x08.

DispatchPirateHunter.note: The crown's own hunter dispatch. strength = clamp(2 - reputation/5, 2, 4) -- the magic at 0x0046568D is `imul 0x66666667` + `sar edx,1`, which is a divide by FIVE. PEMF read this as /10 for a long time and undersized hunters in the mid-reputation band. Duplicate at 0x0045F060.

notice_strip._comment: The game's own notification line along the bottom of the sailing screen. TWO PLAIN GLOBALS -- posting needs no engine call at all. ONE SLOT, NO QUEUE: a post overwrites whatever is showing, so anything sharing it must gate on the counter being 0 or it will eat the game's own news.

text.note: Capacity MEASURED: the next referenced global is 0x00876CF8, exactly +0x100, with 9 referents. The GAME does not respect it -- FUN_004600A0 strcpy's in from the 4096-byte compose buffer unbounded.

ttl.note: Visibility COUNTDOWN, not a timestamp. Set to 100 by the game's own post; decremented once per update tick by FUN_004612B0 at 0x004633B3. Drawn while non-zero.

call_sites._comment: These VAs point at the START OF THE ARGUMENT SETUP, not at the CALL instruction itself -- e.g. divide_plunder 0x00410321 sets up, and the actual `call 0x004F6090` is at 0x0041032A. Verified against Ghidra 2026-08-02.

code_cave._comment: OUT OF SCOPE -- PEMF targets GOG + Steam ONLY. The Challenge Pack (cp-base) is NOT a supported target. Kept for reference only; do not build features on this. Present only in the cp-base/Challenge-Pack exe, NOT in gog-original. Empty (all zero) in cp-base.

ship_record._comment: Overworld ship array at 0x008142F8, stride 0x45C, 256 slots. Slot 0 is the player, 1-7 reserved, 8-255 the AI pool. Offsets below are from the record base.

pursuit_target.note: DEAD END FOR THE PLAYER, measured 2026-08-02 over three runs. Holds a SHIP SLOT INDEX and is the only field that overrides the war-relations check (0x0046A4FC). Written by the engine in exactly one place, 0x0044EF0D inside the convoy builder FUN_0044EB10, always with a slot allocated moments earlier -- NEVER slot 0. Writing 0 persists perfectly and changes nothing: 0 is also the AI's 'no target' sentinel. A ship given target 0 and a ship given no target behaved identically. Do not build on this.

dest_city.note: THE steering lever. A ship whose destination equals its origin has ARRIVED, docks, and is culled in ~2s.

engage_timer.note: Set to 0x96 by the engagement handshake.

engage_with.note: Reciprocal 'who I am fighting'. Written at 0x0046A61E.

hostile_hail.note: Pushed from FUN_004612B0 at 0x0046239A and 0x004628A9 -- the overworld hail from a hostile vessel. Proof the player IS seen by the AI scan.

measured_behaviour._comment: Observed in a running game, not read from code.

ship_culling.note: Ships spawned 2,328-6,315 from the player lived 25s+; ships spawned 11,023-15,492 were culled in 1.8-2.6s. Any 'spawn a ship over there' plan has to respect this.

arrived_ships.note: A spawned ship keeps the factory's destination (its origin port), counts as arrived, docks and is removed in ~2s. Indistinguishable from culling without instrumentation.

overworld_combat.note: Overworld vessels never open fire on the player. Combat begins on player contact. Hostility is real via negative reputation (ports close, hails fire) but no AI ship initiates.

weather._comment: Storms and clouds on the sailing map. Drawn by the overworld tick FUN_004612B0, positioned via FUN_004BBC80, prefabs registered by FUN_00429610.

prefab_cloud.note: The ORDINARY WHITE cloud. Registered one line away from the storm; scaling this one by mistake enlarges fair weather and leaves storms untouched.

storm_scale_site.note: Six bytes = the length of `imul edx, ebx, imm32` (69 D3 imm32), so both instructions can be replaced by one with a tunable operand.

slot_count_site.note: ⛔ 3 IS A HARD CEILING. Positions live in two parallel arrays 0x008B98E4 (x) and 0x008B98F0 (y) that are 12 bytes apart -- exactly three dwords. A 4th slot writes the x array into the y array.

loop_head.note: Weather slot loop. Index in [ESP+0x1c]; slot 0 special-cased at 0x00463563 and is the one the storm uses.

draw_call.sig: __thiscall (prefab, x, y, z, rotMatrix, scale, p7, p8)
draw_call.note: Drawn size = scale * 0.01, written to *(node+0x1c)+0x68. FUN_004BBC10 wraps it and builds the rotation matrix from three binary angles (x 2pi/2^32).

shared_world_scale.note: ⛔ DO NOT scale weather through this. It also feeds the ship AI's engagement distances (FUN_00467F90: *1000 and *0x960).

sounds.files: Assets/Sounds/sailing/Storm.wav, StormBoom.wav, StormYell1/2/Neg-NNN.wav -- all LOOSE on disk, overridable

measured.note: Vanilla storm scale 80. Verified in game to 700 (8.75x) with height 1100, still a defined storm. Scale and height fight: scale 1000 at height 320 washed the whole screen to haze with no visible cloud. Purely visual -- storm gameplay effects not located.

weather_curve.sig: int __cdecl (int x, int y, int playSound)
weather_curve.note: 128000/(dist+4000) over the 3 weather slots, +2000 penalty on slots 1-2. Result cached in 0x0085A0F8, read by 6 sites. Safe to call with playSound=0. Reads POSITIONS, never the drawn scale -- a bigger cloud does not hit harder.

weather_power_site.note: DROP-SIZE dial, NOT drop-count. Measured: 300000 = fat bending bars + 27kt winds; 128000 vanilla; 70000 calmer; 45000 restrained. Also feeds the sailing update, so it changes wind. Denser rain needs the particle COUNT in FUN_0047A040 -- not isolated.

storm_seed.note: Storms are seeded ONCE at (playerX/1e6 + 8, playerY/1e6) * 1000 and never move. The flag is only ever written to ZERO (0x00463587, 0x00471F3A); whatever sets it is a bulk write not yet found. Drifting weather would hook here.

cull_bound_limitation.note: ⚠️ NOT FIXED. Scaling a cloud grows the visual but not the cull sphere, so at high scale the engine drops it while most is still on screen ('disappears once 20-30% off screen'). Offsets derived from Gamebryo 2.6 NiAVObject member order (m_kWorldBound, m_kLocal, m_kWorld) anchored on the known m_kLocal at +0x38. Gamebryo recomputes world bounds during update, so the durable fix is probably the MODEL bound, not the world bound per frame.

instance_pool.note: Prefab keeps a list at +0x10 and allocates another instance when the current is already used this frame (+0x24, set by FUN_004BBC80). Calling the draw again yields ANOTHER cloud, not a moved one -- this is what makes clusters possible. PEMF redirects the call at 0x0046377A. Cluster offsets must be FIXED; per-frame jitter strobes.
